questions.q:
The value of the definite integral
$\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{1}{3^{\frac{x+3}{2}}}\, dx$
is
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{1}{3^x + 3} dx$

Substitute $t = 3^x$, which gives $dt = 3^x \ln 3 dx \Rightarrow dx = \dfrac{dt}{t \ln 3}$.

When $x = 0$, $t = 1$.

When $x = 2$, $t = 9$.

The integral becomes:

$I = \int_{1}^{9} \dfrac{1}{t + 3} \dfrac{dt}{t \ln 3} = \dfrac{1}{\ln 3} \int_{1}^{9} \dfrac{1}{t(t + 3)} dt$

Using partial fractions:

$\dfrac{1}{t(t + 3)} = \dfrac{1}{3} \left( \dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{t + 3} \right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \int_{1}^{9} \left( \dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{t + 3} \right) dt$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} [\ln t - \ln(t + 3)]_{1}^{9}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \left[ \ln\left(\dfrac{t}{t + 3}\right) \right]_{1}^{9}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \left( \ln\left(\dfrac{9}{12}\right) - \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) \right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \left( \ln\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) - \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) \right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \ln\left(\dfrac{3/4}{1/4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \ln 3$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3}$

If $\alpha=\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^2 \frac{\tan ^{-1} x}{2 x^2-3 x+2} d x$ 
then the value of $\sqrt{7} \tan \left(\frac{2 \alpha \sqrt{7}}{\pi}\right)$ is ____________.
(Here, the $inverse trigonometric function\tan ^{-1} x$ assumes values in $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.)
questions.solution:
$\alpha=\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^2 \frac{\tan ^{-1} x}{2 x^2-3 x+2} d x$ ....(i)
$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } x=\frac{1}{t} \\ & \qquad d x=-\frac{1}{t^2} d t \\ & \alpha=\int_2^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{t}\right)}{\frac{2}{t^2}-\frac{3}{t}+2}\left(\frac{-1}{t^2}\right) d t\end{aligned} \alpha=\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^2 \frac{\cot ^{-1} \mathrm{t}}{2 \mathrm{t}^2-3 \mathrm{t}+2} \mathrm{dt}$ ....(ii)
Now by (i) + (ii)
$\begin{aligned}
& 2 \alpha=\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^2 \frac{\frac{\pi}{2}}{2 x^2-3 x+2} d x \\
& \alpha=\frac{\pi}{8} \int_{\frac{1}{2}}^2 \frac{d x}{x^2-\frac{3 x}{2}+1} \\
& \alpha=\frac{\pi}{8} \int_{\frac{1}{2}}^2\left(x-\frac{3}{4}\right)^2+\frac{7}{16} \\
& \alpha=\frac{\pi}{8 \times \frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}}\left[\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x-\frac{3}{4}}{\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}}\right)\right]_{\frac{1}{2}}^2
\end{aligned} \begin{aligned}
& \alpha=\frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{7}}\left[\tan ^{-1} \frac{4 x-3}{\sqrt{7}}\right]_{\frac{1}{2}}^2 \\
& \alpha=\frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{7}}\left[\tan ^{-1} \frac{5}{\sqrt{7}}-\tan ^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\right)\right] \\
& \alpha=\frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{7}} \tan ^{-1} \frac{\left(\frac{5}{\sqrt{7}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\right)}{1-\frac{5}{7}} \\
& \alpha=\frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{7}} \tan ^{-1}(3 \sqrt{7})
\end{aligned}$
Now $\sqrt{7} \tan \left(\frac{2 \sqrt{7} \alpha}{\pi}\right) \begin{aligned}
& \sqrt{7} \times \tan \left(\tan ^{-1}(3 \sqrt{7})\right) \\
& \sqrt{7} \times 3 \sqrt{7} \\
& =21
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x\tan^{- 1}x}\dfrac{{e}^{\left(t - cost\right)}}{1 + {t}^{2023}}dt$

Now differentiating both side we get,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{e}^{\left[x\tan^{- 1}x - cos\left(x\tan^{- 1}x\right)\right]}}{1 + {\left(x\tan^{- 1}x\right)}^{2023}} \times \left(\dfrac{x}{1 + {x}^{2}} + \tan^{- 1}x\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = g\left(x\right) \cdot h\left(x\right)$

$\text{where}g\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{e}^{\left[x\tan^{- 1} ⁡ x - cos ⁡ \left(x\tan^{- 1} ⁡ x\right)\right]}}{1 + {\left(x\tan^{- 1} ⁡ x\right)}^{2023}} > 0∀x$

And $h\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{1 + {x}^{2}} + \tan^{- 1}x\text{which is}\left\{\begin{array}{ll} 0x > 0\end{array}\right$

$∴ f\left(x\right)$ has minimum at $x = 0$

And $f{\left(x\right)}_{min} = f\left(0\right) = 0$

Consider the equation

${∫}_{1}^{e}\dfrac{{\left({\log}_{e}x\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}{x{\left(a - {\left({\log}_{e}x\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}\right)}^{2}}dx = 1, a \in \left(- \infty , 0\right) ∪ \left(1, \infty\right)$.

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
options: No a satisfies the above equation
An integer a satisfies the above equation
An irrational number a satisfies the above equation
More than one a satisfy the above equation
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{1}^{e}\dfrac{{\left(lnx\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}dx}{x{\left(a - {\left(lnx\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}\right)}^{2}}$

Now put $a - \left(lnx\right)\dfrac{3}{2} = t$

$⇒ - \dfrac{3}{2}\left(lnx\right)\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x}dx = dt$

So, the integral becomes $I = {∫}_{a}^{a - 1}\dfrac{\left(- \dfrac{2}{3}\right)dt}{{t}^{2}}$

$⇒ I = \left(- \dfrac{2}{3}\right){\dfrac{{t}^{- 2 + 1}}{- 2 + 1}}_{a}^{a - 1}$

$⇒ I = {\dfrac{2}{3t}}_{a}^{a - 1}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{a - 1} - \dfrac{1}{a}\right)$

Now given $I = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\dfrac{1}{a\left(a - 1\right)} = 1$

$⇒ 2 = 3{a}^{2} - 3a$

$⇒ 3{a}^{2} - 3a - 2 = 0$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{9 - 4\left(3\right)\left(- 2\right)}}{6}$

So, $a = \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{33}}{6}, \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{33}}{6}$

Let $f: \left[- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right] \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function such that $f\left(0\right) = 1$ and ${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}f\left(t\right)dt = 0$

Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
options: The equation $f\left(x\right) - 3cos3x = 0$ has at least one solution in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$
The equation $f\left(x\right) - 3sin3x = - \dfrac{6}{\pi}$ has at least one solution in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$
questions.solution:
(A) Let $g\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right) - 3cos3x$

Now

${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}g\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}f\left(x\right)dx - 3{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}cos3xdx$

$= 0 - {\left[sin3x\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} = 0$

Hence $g\left(x\right) = 0$ has a root in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

(B) Let $h\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right) - 3sin3x + \dfrac{6}{\pi}$

Now

${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}h\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}f\left(x\right)dx - 3{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}sin3xdx + {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\dfrac{6}{\pi}dx$

$= 0 - {\left[- cos3x\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} + {\left[\dfrac{6x}{\pi}\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}$

$= 0 - 2 + 2 = 0$

Hence $h\left(x\right) = 0$has a root in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

(C) $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x{∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt}{1 - {e}^{{x}^{2}}}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\mathop{\mathop{\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{1 - {e}^{{x}^{2}}}\right) \times}_{⏟}}_{- 1}\mathop{\mathop{\left(\dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{x}f( t )dt}{x}\right)}_{⏟}}_{Apply{L}^{'}hospitalrule}\right)$

$= - 1\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{1} = - 1$

(D) $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{( sinx ) {∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt}{{x}^{2}}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\mathop{\mathop{\left(\dfrac{sinx}{x}\right)}_{⏟}}_{1} \times \mathop{\mathop{\left(\dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{x}f( t )dt}{x}\right)}_{⏟}}_{Apply{L}^{'}hospitalrule}\right)$

$= 1\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{1} = 1$

Define

$$

S_{i}=\int_{\frac{\pi}{8}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{8}} f(x) \cdot g_{i}(x) d x, \quad i=1,2

$$

The value of $\dfrac{16{S}_{1}}{\pi}$ is ___.
questions.solution:
${S}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{8}}^{\dfrac{3\pi}{8}}\sin^{2}x \cdot 1dx \ldots \ldots . . . \left(i\right)$

${S}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{8}}^{\dfrac{3\pi}{8}}\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8} + \dfrac{\pi}{8} - x\right)dx$

${S}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{8}}^{\dfrac{3\pi}{8}}\cos^{2}xdx \ldots \ldots . . \left(ii\right)$

From (i) and (ii), we get

$2{S}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{8}}^{\dfrac{3\pi}{8}}1dx$

$2{S}_{1} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$\dfrac{16{S}_{1}}{\pi} = 2$

Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that its derivative ${f}^{'}$ is continuous and $f\left(\pi\right) = - 6$. If $F: \left[0, \pi\right] \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt,$ and if

${∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left({f}^{'}\left(x\right) + F\left(x\right)\right)cosxdx = 2$, then the value of $f\left(0\right)$ is_______
questions.solution:
$I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left({f}^{'}\left(x\right) \cdot cosx + F\left(x\right) \cdot cosx\right)dx = 2$

$= {∫}_{0}^{\pi}{f}^{'}\left(x\right) \cdot cosx \cdot dx + {∫}_{0}^{\pi}F\left(x\right)cosx \cdot dx = 2$

$= {\left(cosx \cdot f ( x )\right)}_{0}^{\pi} - {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(- sinx\right) \cdot f\left(x\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{\pi}F\left(x\right) \cdot cosx \cdot dx = 2$

$⇒ \left(cos\pi . f\left(\pi\right) - cos0 . f\left(0\right)\right) + {∫}_{0}^{\pi}sinx \cdot f\left(x\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{\pi}F\left(x\right) \cdot cosxdx = 2$

$⇒ \left(\left(- 1\right) \cdot \left(- 6\right) - f\left(0\right)\right) + {\left(sinx . F ( x )\right)}_{0}^{\pi} - {∫}_{0}^{\pi}cosx \cdot F\left(x\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{\pi}F\left(x\right) \cdot cosx \cdot dx = 2$

$⇒ 6 - f\left(0\right) + \left(sin\pi \cdot F\left(\pi\right) - sin0 . F\left(0\right)\right) = 2$

$⇒ f\left(0\right) = 4$.

We know that $cosx = 1 - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} + \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4 !} - \dfrac{{x}^{6}}{6 !} + \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots$

$⇒ cosx \ge 1 - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}$

$∴ {∫}_{0}^{1}xcosxdx \ge {∫}_{0}^{1}x\left(1 - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)dx = {\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{8}\right)}_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{3}{8}$

So, option $\left(A\right)$ is correct.

Now, we also know that $sinx = x - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3 !} + \dfrac{{x}^{5}}{5 !} - \dfrac{{x}^{7}}{7 !} + \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots$

$⇒ sinx \ge x - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3 !}, x \in \left[0, 1\right]

$∴ {∫}_{0}^{1}xsinxdx \ge {∫}_{0}^{1}x $\left(x - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{6}\right)$dx = {$\left(\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{{x}^{5}}{6 \times 5}\right)$}_{0}^{1} = $\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{9}{30} = \dfrac{3}{10}

So, option \left(B\right) is correct.

Now, ${∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}cosxdx \ge {∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}$\left(1 - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)$dx = {$\left(\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{{x}^{5}}{2 \times 5}\right)$}_{0}^{1} = $\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{7}{30}

Also, ${x}^{2}cosx \le {x}^{2}$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}cosxdx \le {∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}dx$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}cosxdx \le {$\left(\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right)$}_{0}^{1} = $\dfrac{1}{3}

So, \dfrac{7}{30}$ \le {∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}cosxdx \le $\dfrac{1}{3}$

Now, ${∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}sinxdx \ge {∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\left(x - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3 !}\right)dx = {\left(\dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4} - \dfrac{{x}^{6}}{6 \times 6}\right)}_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{36} = \dfrac{8}{36} = \dfrac{2}{9}$

So, option $\left(D\right)$ is correct.

Now, if we take $c=\frac{a+b}{2}$, then using above again, we get $\int_a^b f(x) d x=\int_a^c f(x) d x+\int_c^b f(x) d x \cong \frac{b-a}{4}\{f(a)+f(b)+2 f(c)\}$ and so on. We get approximation for value of $\int_a^b f(x) d x$.Question: Good approximation of $\int_0^{\pi / 2} \sin x d x$, is
questions.explanation: $\int_0^{\pi / 2} \sin x d x=\frac{\frac{\pi}{2}-0}{4}\left(\sin 0+\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+2 \sin \left(\frac{0+\frac{\pi}{2}}{2}\right)\right)=\frac{\pi}{8}(1+\sqrt{2})$.
